# Electromagnetic waves and radio (`electromagnetic_waves_radio`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/electricity.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Electricity & electronics (`electricity`)
- Deps: needs electromagnetism; helped by calculus, speed_of_light, wave_nature_light_sound, crystal_detector, vacuum_tube, static_electricity
- Core idea: A changing electric current sends out waves of electric and magnetic force that travel through empty space at the speed of light; light is such a wave of very short wavelength. A spark jumping across a gap between two metal rods, fed by an induction coil, radiates waves whose length is about twice the length of the rods, and they produce a tiny spark in a similar gapped loop or rod some metres away. For signalling, connect one side of the spark gap to a long elevated wire and the other to earth, and at the receiver join aerial and earth through a coil and condenser tuned to the same frequency and a detector with an earphone. Wavelength equals the speed of light divided by frequency, and a coil and condenser resonate at one frequency fixed by their sizes.
- Pitfalls:
  - Thinking radio waves are sound waves or need air; they are of the same nature as light and cross a vacuum
  - No tuning: an untuned spark transmitter fills the whole spectrum and every station disturbs every other
  - Expecting short waves to follow the curve of the earth; long distances depend on long waves hugging the ground or on reflection from the upper atmosphere, which nobody predicted
  - Sending speech with sparks; speech needs a continuous wave (arc, alternator or valve oscillator) whose strength is varied
  - Calling Marconi the inventor of radio; Maxwell, Hertz, Lodge, Bose, Popov, Braun and Tesla all contributed, and Marconi made it a working long-distance system
- History: europe: 1864–1865 – Maxwell predicts the waves and identifies light with them; 1887–1888 Hertz produces and measures them (Karlsruhe); 1894 Lodge signals with a coherer; 1895 Popov's receiver (St Petersburg); 1895–1896 Marconi signals over kilometres (Bologna, then England); india: 1894–1895 – J. C. Bose in Calcutta generates and detects millimetre waves and rings a bell through walls at a public demonstration; americas: 1901 – Marconi reports receiving a signal across the Atlantic in Newfoundland (doubted by some physicists then and now); 1906 Fessenden transmits speech with an alternator; 1920 regular broadcasting (KDKA, Pittsburgh)
- Read:
  - James Clerk Maxwell, A Dynamical Theory of the Electromagnetic Field, Philosophical Transactions 155 (1865)
  - Heinrich Hertz, Electric Waves (1893)
  - Sungook Hong, Wireless: From Marconi's Black-Box to the Audion (2001)
